- **Measure the impact** [in production]: After a release I watch metrics and regressions; ClickStack alerts reach Telegram with deduplication. In the summary bot users vote on quality, and the prompt changes based on that data.

- **RAG and knowledge-base search** [in projects]: Qwen3 embeddings and clustering of 3600 vacancies; ranking by similarity to past applications. The search on this site (⌘K) works as a RAG retrieval layer right in the browser.

- **LangChain / LangGraph** [closing the gap]: I write agent loops myself: state, tools, checkpoints, retries. That is the same model as a LangGraph state graph, so moving to your stack is quick.
- **Vector databases** [closing the gap]: I have done embeddings, nearest-neighbour search and clustering in my own projects. A dedicated vector DB (pgvector) goes into the supplier demo in part two.

## Projects

### Finance AI agent and deposit orchestrator (Askloyal · B2C → B2B, 2026)
- Problem: Users kept dollars idle and decided by hand where to move them for yield. Slow, risky, and it does not scale to B2B partners.
- Built: An orchestrator that spreads deposits across pools for the best yield: up to 17% APY versus 7% in a regular bank, with no FX risk.
- Built: An LLM agent that proposes financial actions. Guardrails: it executes only what we marked safe, everything else needs confirmation.
- Built: Reliability: workers, retries, idempotency, daily reconciliation, alerts.
- Built: Integrations with B2B partners who bring their own customers.
- Result: Launched in July, 2000 users in the first week, now 8000 users and $600k AUM. The code is open on GitHub.
- Stack: Rust, Go, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, ClickStack, LLM agent, Solana
- Link: https://github.com/loyal-labs/loyal-app

### Telegram chat summaries that learn from votes (Askloyal · LLM in the product, 2026)
- Problem: Finance chats get hundreds of messages a day. People miss what matters, and nobody will write a digest by hand.
- Built: A bot posts a daily or weekly summary into each chat, with an image.
- Built: Members vote summaries up or down. Votes become a dataset that drives prompt changes: an auto-research loop.
- Result: This maps directly to your needs: regular digests, reports and personalized messaging with a feedback loop.
- Stack: TypeScript, Telegram Bot API, LLM, image generation

### Rewrote a service with agents and proved nothing broke (Askloyal · Rust → Go, 2026)
- Problem: The planner and revalidator had to move from Rust to Go. Agents write the code, so we needed a check we can trust, not "seems to work".
- Built: The old Rust code became the reference. Both versions get the same inputs and are compared on exact output.
- Built: Fixtures, disposable PostgreSQL, mutation controls: the harness catches skipped, duplicated and fabricated agent "successes".
- Result: 154 of 154 scenarios matched. This is how I would run AI pilots for you: success criteria first, code second.
- Stack: Go, Rust, PostgreSQL, differential testing

### Automated my own job search (Personal project · end to end, 2026)
- Problem: Vacancies on HH, Habr Career, LinkedIn and Himalayas, applications, chats, statuses. By hand that is hours a day, and things get lost.
- Built: A Chrome extension (MV3) collects vacancies and chats in my own browser profile, paced so it never hammers the sites.
- Built: Native messaging → Python → Google Sheets API: one atomic write, a concurrent-edit check, read-back verification.
- Built: Profile-based scoring, an HTML dashboard and a macOS widget: one button runs the whole thing.
- Built: Guardrails: it never submits applications by itself and stops at any captcha.
- Result: 3604 vacancies collected and ranked automatically. That is how I found your vacancy.
- Stack: Python, Chrome MV3, Google Sheets API, Swift / WidgetKit, Codex, Pi

### Semantic vacancy atlas (Embeddings · local models, 2026)
- Problem: Keywords can't tell "AI engineer" from "AI marketer". You need search by meaning.
- Built: Qwen3 embeddings via Ollama, run locally with no data leaving the machine.
- Built: UMAP and HDBSCAN lay out vacancies on a 3D cluster map.
- Built: Final score: 60% profile rules plus 40% similarity to vacancies I already applied to.
- Result: The same approach works for smart search in your ERP: meaning, not exact word match.
- Stack: Python, Ollama, Qwen3 embeddings, UMAP, HDBSCAN

### Slip: receipt recognition (Android · offline, 2026)
- Problem: Receipts and waybills arrive as photos. Retyping line items is slow and errors break the reports.
- Built: Photo → Russian and English OCR → a review screen where a person fixes items → SQLite.
- Built: SHA-256 dedup, weekly, monthly and category reports, export.
- Built: Built by an agent in a day, with E2E tests on an emulator.
- Result: A template for your invoices and waybills: recognize, let a person verify, store the structure.
- Stack: Android, ML Kit, Tesseract, SQLite, E2E tests

### My own tools for agents (pi-rs · Pi Remote · usage widget, 2026)
- Problem: Off-the-shelf agents are good, but each project needs them tuned, and sometimes rewritten.
- Built: pi-rs: an agent harness in Rust with model providers, tools, context compaction and a TUI.
- Built: Pi Remote: an Android client that drives agents on several machines, with end-to-end encryption.
- Built: A macOS widget that shows remaining Codex and Claude limits per account.
- Result: I understand agents from the inside: why they lose context, how to restrict tools and how to check their work.
- Stack: Rust, TypeScript, Python, Android, Swift, MCP

### Noise-free alerts in Telegram (Askloyal · internal tool, 2026)
- Problem: Monitoring alerts either get lost or flood the chat with duplicates.
- Built: A ClickStack → Telegram relay: dedup by eventId and a one-hour cooldown.
- Result: The team sees every incident once, right away.
- Stack: TypeScript, ClickStack, Telegram Bot API

## Pilots proposed for the Goulash ERP (synthetic demos on the site)
- Smart ERP search: The owner asks in plain words. The agent picks tools, queries ERP data and answers with sources. How to measure: share of questions answered without a support call; time to answer; 👍/👎 under every answer. Pilot: 5 venues, 2 weeks.
- Guest auto-segmentation: K-means runs right here on 600 synthetic guests by order frequency and average check. An LLM then names segments and writes a personal offer. How to measure: A/B against the current campaign, conversion to order and revenue per recipient. 10% holdout.
- Kitchen load risks: Hourly order forecast against kitchen capacity. Move the cooks slider: overloaded hours light up and the agent writes an alert for the manager. How to measure: late orders and ticket time in hours where the alert fired versus similar hours without it.

## How I work
1. Talk to people: First understand how the process works today and where it hurts. At my first job the users of my tool sat next door, the best feedback loop there is.
2. Success criteria: A metric and a check before code: what counts as success, on which data, and how we will notice a regression.
3. Simple first: The simplest version that delivers value. Then improve based on feedback, not the other way round.
4. Agents + harness: I write code with agents in an implement/verify loop. The harness rejects fabricated "done".
5. Guardrails: The agent can only do what is safe. Money, outgoing messages and deletions go through a person.
6. Ship and measure: Monitoring, alerts, A/B. Keep what worked and scale it.
